evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.150: attentiōne animī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Not a common word: Latin mostly says it with a verb, animum attendere or operam dare, and an attentive listener is attentus.

evidence: Ter. Ph. 30: date operam, adeste aequō animō

terms.gloss: pay attention, turn one’s mind to
evidence: Ter. Ph. 24: nunc quid velim animum attendite
Cic. Off. 1.103: excitanda animadversiō et dīligentia (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Also censure or punishment, from animadvertere in aliquem.

phrases.latin: date operam, cum silentiō animum attendite
phrases.english: give us your attention, and listen in silence

phrases.latin: videō, patrēs cōnscrīptī, in mē omnium vestrum ōra atque oculōs esse conversōs
phrases.english: I see, members of the senate, that all your faces and eyes are turned on me

sources: Lewis & Short: attentio · Lewis & Short: opera · Lewis & Short: attendo · Lewis & Short: animadversio · Lewis & Short: converto
